title: Unsupervised Learning & Clustering
subtitle: K-means, DBSCAN, PCA, and finding hidden structure

content.text: Clustering groups similar data points without labels. K-means partitions data into K clusters by minimising within-cluster variance.

content.code:
from sklearn.cluster import KMeans, DBSCAN
from sklearn.decomposition import PCA
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# K-means
kmeans = KMeans(n_clusters=4, random_state=42)
labels = kmeans.fit_predict(X)

# DBSCAN (density-based, handles arbitrary shapes)
db = DBSCAN(eps=0.5, min_samples=10)
db_labels = db.fit_predict(X)

# PCA for visualisation
pca = PCA(n_components=2)
X_2d = pca.fit_transform(X)
plt.scatter(X_2d[:,0], X_2d[:,1], c=labels)
plt.show()

content.text: Use the elbow method (inertia vs K) to choose K for K-means.

questions.question: What is a key advantage of DBSCAN over K-means?
options: DBSCAN finds clusters of arbitrary shape and identifies outliers
DBSCAN works better on high-dimensional data
questions.explanation: DBSCAN can find clusters of any shape and labels outliers as noise, unlike K-means which assumes spherical clusters.

faq.q: How do I evaluate clustering quality without labels?
faq.a: Use the Silhouette score (how similar a point is to its cluster vs other clusters). Values near 1 are good.
